blocks.heading: WELCOME — DAY 4
blocks.board_text:
Student Mode · Day 4 of 5

Today: Compute and Storage — EC2 + S3

We will cover:
• EC2 as rented virtual computers
• S3 as object storage for files
• How real apps use both together
blocks.ren_voice: Welcome Day 4. Identity and network ready. Inniku rendu services — almost every app use panradhu: EC2 compute — code run panna virtual computer — and S3 storage — files, images, backups. Run versus store clear aanaa, AWS architecture click aagum. Same class flow. Mental model build panrom.

blocks.heading: WHAT ARE EC2 AND S3?
blocks.board_text:
EC2 = Elastic Compute Cloud
A virtual computer you rent by the hour.
You choose: CPU, RAM, operating system, network placement.
It runs your code. You pay only while it's running.

S3 = Simple Storage Service
Virtually unlimited file storage.
You create a bucket, upload files, access them via URL.
You pay per GB stored per month.

Together:
EC2 runs it. S3 stores it.
Almost every application on AWS uses both.
blocks.ren_voice: Rendu services — ithai purinjitaa, most applications-oda core purinjuduvaanga. EC2, AWS-la irundhu rent panna oru virtual computer. Eppadi powerful-nu namba decide pannuvom — how many CPUs, how much RAM — OS-um choose pannuvom. AWS andha machine start pannum, namba code adha-la run pannuvom. Per hour pay pannuvom, anytime stop panna mudiyum. S3, file storage. Database illai — files vaikkara place. Images, videos, log files, config files, backups. Bucket create pannuvom — AWS-oda container-ku bucket-nu peyar — files upload pannuvom, URL or API-la accessible. Per gigabyte per month pay pannuvom. EC2 code run pannum. S3 files hold pannum. Rendu serndhaa, AWS-la run aagura most applications-oda behind irukku.

check_question.question: In one sentence each — what does EC2 do, and what does S3 do?
check_question.ren_response_if_correct: Exactly — EC2 compute, code run panna computer. S3 storage, files vaikkara idham. Difference matter: EC2 active processing, S3 persistent storage. Different things panniduvaanga, serndhu use panna vendiyadhu.
check_question.ren_response_if_incorrect: Simple-a solren. EC2 computer — code run pannum, requests process pannum, work pannum. S3 filing cabinet — files hold pannum, yaaravadhu venum-nu irundha edutthukkuvaanga. EC2 active, S3 storage. Difference clear-a theriyudaa?

blocks.heading: WHY EC2 AND S3 SPECIFICALLY?
blocks.board_text:
Without EC2:
• You buy physical servers — weeks to procure, crores of rupees upfront
• Server sits idle at full cost during low-traffic periods
• Scaling takes months, not minutes

Without S3:
• Files live on EC2 servers — if a server crashes, the files go with it
• Scaling storage means buying more hardware
• No shared access between multiple servers

With EC2 + S3:
• EC2: start a server in minutes, pay by the hour, scale instantly
• S3: files survive server crashes, accessible from anywhere, effectively infinite capacity
blocks.ren_voice: EC2 illaadhappo alternative, physical server vangaradhu. Weeks to procure, significant capital upfront, physically maintain panna yaravadhu venum, busy-a illaadhappo kuda full cost pay pannanum. EC2 ellathaiyum remove panniduchu — server venum, two minutes, done. S3 illaadhappo alternative, EC2 servers-la files store pannardhu. Critical problem create aaguchu — andha server crash aanalaa, restart aanalaa, replace aanalaa, files pogum. S3 storage-a compute-la irundhu completely separate panniduchu. Files S3-la, independent of any server. Account-la every EC2 instance terminated aanalum, S3-la files still there. Andha independence-taan S3, namba keep panna venum-na edhuvum correct place.

check_question.question: A developer stores user-uploaded photos directly on the EC2 server's local disk. What is the risk?
check_question.ren_response_if_correct: Exactly — EC2 instance stop aanalaa, replace aanalaa, crash aanalaa, photos pogum. EC2 local disk temporary. S3-taan persist vendiyadhukku correct place, any specific server-la independent.
check_question.ren_response_if_incorrect: EC2 server stop or terminate aanappo andha server-oda local disk-ku enna aagum-nu yosinga. Disk permanent illai — server pogum, disk-um pogum. Andha-la store panra photo-um disappear. S3, any individual server-a outlast panna vendiya files-ukku specifically design panna — adhu-taan separation matter.

blocks.heading: HOW EC2 AND S3 WORK — THE MENTAL MODELS
blocks.board_text:
EC2 mental model:
You pick a size (t3.micro = small, m5.large = medium, c5.xlarge = large).
You pick an OS (Amazon Linux, Ubuntu).
You pick a VPC and subnet (from Day 3).
You boot it. Your code runs on it.

S3 mental model:
You create a bucket (a named container, globally unique).
You upload files. Each file gets a URL.
No disk management. No size limit. Pay per GB.

EC2 + S3 together:
EC2 code receives a file upload → stores it in S3 → saves the S3 URL in the database
EC2 code needs to display a file → gets the URL from database → browser loads it from S3
blocks.ren_voice: EC2 mental model: size pick pannuvaanga — instance type. t3.micro, small machine, low-traffic apps-ku good. m5.large, medium machine, typical backend workloads-ku. c5.xlarge, compute-heavy, processing-intensive jobs-ku. OS choose pannuvaanga — Amazon Linux or Ubuntu common. VPC and subnet choose pannuvaanga — yesterday paaththadhu network placement. Boot pannuvaanga, code run aaguchu. S3 mental model: bucket create pannuvaanga — named container. Peyar globally unique across all of AWS. Files upload pannuvaanga, each file-ku URL kidaikkum. Disk manage panna illai, size limit yosikka illai. Per gigabyte per month pay pannuvaanga. EC2 and S3 serndhu: user photo upload pannuvaan, EC2 server receive pannum, S3-la store pannum, S3 URL database-la save pannum. Apparam andha photo display panna, EC2 database-la irundhu URL get pannum, browser directly S3-la irundhu photo load pannum. EC2 file-yae thodalavae thodalai — URL mattum vachu irukku.

check_question.question: When a user uploads a profile photo through your app, which service receives the file and which service stores it long-term?
check_question.ren_response_if_correct: Right — EC2 file receive pannum (application code run panna EC2-la irukkum), apparam S3-ku permanent storage-ku anuppuchu. EC2 S3 URL database-la save pannum. File itself S3-la irukkum. Andha separation-taan pattern.
check_question.ren_response_if_incorrect: Oru service-oda role yosinga. EC2 application code run panniduchu — user yedhaavadhu upload pannaa, namba code on EC2 receive pannum. Aana code immediately file-a S3-la permanent storage-ku poduvaan, yen-naa EC2 disk-la vaikka vidam illai. EC2 S3 URL database-la keep pannum. File S3-la irukkum.

blocks.heading: WHAT THIS LOOKS LIKE IN THE AWS CONSOLE
blocks.board_text:
EC2 console:
→ Services → Compute → EC2 → Instances
→ 'Launch Instance' — choose AMI (OS), instance type (size), VPC, subnet, key pair
→ Running instances: you see state (running/stopped), instance type, public/private IP, which AZ
→ Instance types dropdown: t3.micro, t3.small, m5.large, c5.xlarge — each with CPU and RAM listed

S3 console:
→ Services → Storage → S3 → Buckets
→ 'Create Bucket' — choose name and region
→ Inside a bucket: list of files (objects), each with a URL, size, last modified
→ Upload button: drag files in, they appear in the list with a URL immediately
blocks.ren_voice: EC2 console: Services → Compute → EC2 → Instances. Ellaa running and stopped instances-oda list — state, type, public and private IP, which Availability Zone. Launch Instance click pannaa oru wizard varum: AMI choose pannuveenga — OS image; instance type choose pannuveenga, CPU and RAM size dropdown-la; VPC and subnet choose pannuveenga; key pair configure pannuveenga. S3 console: Services → Storage → S3. Ellaa buckets list paappeenga. Oru bucket click pannaa, ulayey files — key, size, last modified date, URL. Create Bucket click pannaa, name, region, access settings configure pannuveenga. Console-la file drag pannaa, immediately list-la URL-oda appear aaguchu. Rendu consoles-um workspace-la navigate panuveengaa.

check_question.question: In the EC2 console, where would you go to see all currently running servers in your account?
check_question.ren_response_if_correct: Correct — EC2 → Instances. Andha list, every instance, current state, type, network details show pannum. Almost every EC2 task-ku starting point adhu.
check_question.ren_response_if_incorrect: Path: Services → EC2 → Instances. Account-la every instance-oda full list — running, stopped, terminated. Instances view, EC2 work-oda home base.

blocks.heading: YOUR TURN — WHAT WOULD YOU DO?
blocks.board_text:
Scenario:
Your team is deploying a food delivery app with three parts:
• A Node.js backend API that handles orders
• A React frontend (static HTML, CSS, JS files)
• Customer profile photos uploaded by users

Which parts go on EC2?
Which parts go in S3?
Is there anything that goes in neither?
blocks.ren_voice: Real deployment question. Moonu components: Node.js backend API, React frontend, customer profile photos. Enna-la each one irukkaanum — EC2-aa S3-aa. Yosinga — each component actually enna, enna panna vendiyathu, run aagura code-aa illa store aagura files-aa.

check_question.question: Walk me through your placement decision for each of the three components — and why.
check_question.ren_response_if_correct: Exactly right — Node.js backend EC2-la, requests process panna code run panniduchu. React frontend static files, S3-la directly serve panna mudiyum, speed-ku CloudFront front-la. Customer photos S3-la, user-generated files any server-la independent-a persist vendiyadhu. Moondrum correct-a sonna.
check_question.ren_response_if_incorrect: Work through pannuvom. Node.js backend — run aagura code, requests process pannum, database-kku talk pannum. Adhu EC2. React frontend — HTML, CSS, JavaScript files. Andha files server-la run aagaadhu, browsers-ku serve aagum. Adhu S3. Customer photos — user-generated files, persist vendiyadhu. S3. Each component-ku key question: run aagura code-aa, illa file-aa?

blocks.heading: WHAT HAPPENS WHEN YOU GET THE INSTANCE TYPE WRONG
blocks.board_text:
A real mistake:
A team chose a t3.micro EC2 instance for their production database server.
Reason: it was the cheapest option.

What happened on launch day:
• Real user traffic arrived
• t3.micro uses CPU credits — it can burst, but sustained load drains credits fast
• 2 hours after launch, CPU credits were exhausted
• Database queries slowed from 20ms to 30 seconds
• App appeared broken to users
• Emergency: upgrade instance type, which required downtime

The instance type was correct for development. It was wrong for production.
blocks.ren_voice: Real scenario. Oru startup production database-ku t3.micro EC2 instance choose pannaa — list-la cheapest option-nu. Development and testing-la fine-a irundhu — traffic low, instance handle panniduchu. Real users-oda launch day vandhu. Two hours-la, t3.micro-oda CPU credit balance exhaust aaguchu. t3.micro burstable instance — baseline-ku mela credits use panni short periods-la perform panna mudiyum, aana sustained load credits drain panniduchu. Credits run out aanappo CPU throttle aaguchu, real load-oda production database-ku far too low. 20 milliseconds aarana queries 30 seconds aachu. User perspective-la app broken. Fix: instance stop pannanum, instance type m5.large-maathiri appropriate-ku change pannanum, restart — downtime. Instance type decision, cost mattum illai. Workload fit pathi.

check_question.question: What should the team have considered when choosing the instance type for a production database — beyond just the hourly price?
check_question.ren_response_if_correct: Right — real production load-la sustained CPU and memory requirements, development load-la illai. t3.micro bursts handle panna mudiyum, aana continuous production traffic-oda database-ku sustained performance venum, burst credits illai. Instance type choice, workload-oda steady-state requirements-ku match pannanum.
check_question.ren_response_if_incorrect: 'Development-ku cheap enough' and 'production-ku right' difference yosinga. Development database low, intermittent traffic paakkum. Production database continuous load paakkum. t3 family burstable — light, intermittent workloads-ku works. Sustained, continuous workloads-ku, production database-ku, m5 family maathiri consistent CPU tharum instance type venum, burst credits illai.

blocks.heading: QUICK CHALLENGE
blocks.board_text:
A new engineer on your team has set an S3 bucket containing customer invoices to Public access.

You discover this. What do you do first, and what does that action actually prevent?
blocks.ren_voice: Customer invoices — sensitive financial documents — irukkaara bucket Public-a set pannaacha. Yaarum URL-a ithandha invoices download panna mudiyum. First enna panreenga, andha action actually enna prevent pannum?

check_question.question: What is your first action, and what specifically does it prevent?
check_question.ren_response_if_correct: Right — immediately bucket-la Block Public Access enable pannu. Andha bucket-la irukkaara objects-ku yedha public access-um prevent pannum, individual files-ku public permissions set aanalum. Adhu master switch. Piragu, yaravadhu accessed panna-nu audit pannuvaanga, data exposed aanaa notify pannuvaanga, policy review implement pannuvaanga.
check_question.ren_response_if_incorrect: First action: S3 Block Public Access andha bucket-la enable pannu. Ithu master switch — object-level permissions override pannum, veyra-la enna set aanalum, any public access prevent pannum. Second action: S3 access logs check pannu, public-a irunna window-la yedhaavadhu invoices actually download aanaa-nu. First prevent, then investigate.

blocks.heading: HOW ZOMATO USES EC2 AND S3
blocks.board_text:
Zomato — Indian food delivery platform:

• Restaurant photos, menu images, delivery partner photos → S3
• Backend API servers processing orders, menus, reviews → EC2 behind a load balancer
• EC2 instances behind an ALB across multiple AZs — if one AZ fails, traffic reroutes
• S3 costs a fraction of a rupee per GB. EC2 scales with demand.
• Traffic flow: user request → load balancer → EC2 → fetch S3 URL from database → return to browser → browser loads image from S3
• EC2 never touches the image file itself — just the URL
blocks.ren_voice: Zomato, EC2 and S3 serndhu scale-la work panra clear example. Zomato-la ninga paakkaara every image — restaurant photos, dish photos, delivery partner profile photos — S3-la store aaguchu. Ninga oru restaurant page open pannaa, request load balancer-ku poguchu, Zomato backend run panna EC2 instances-la oru-ku route aaguchu. EC2 server database query pannum, photos-oda S3 URLs list edukuchu, response-la return pannum. Browser directly S3-la irundhu each image load pannum — EC2 actual image file thodalavae thodalai, just address. Backend API servers EC2-la, load balancer-oda behind, multiple Availability Zones-la — oru AZ down aanaalum traffic automatically veyra-ku route aaguchu. S3 gigabyte-ku fraction of a rupee. EC2 incoming traffic-ku based-a scale aaguchu. Rendu independently scale aaguchu — adhu correct design.

lesson_summary.board_text:
What you must know after Day 4:

• EC2 = virtual computer — runs your code, pay by the hour, choose size and OS
• S3 = unlimited file storage — pay per GB, files persist independently of servers
• Never store user-generated files on EC2 local disk — use S3
• Instance type choice matters: burstable (t3) for light workloads, general purpose (m5) for sustained production load
• EC2 and S3 work together: EC2 runs the code, S3 holds the files, database holds the URLs
lesson_summary.ren_voice: Day 4 aavudhu. EC2 virtual computer — code run pannuvaanga, per hour pay pannuvaanga, workload-ku match panna size choose pannuvaanga. S3 storage layer — files, images, backups, any server-la independent-a persist vendiyadhu. Most important thing: EC2 local disk-la files store pannaadheenga. S3 use pannunga. Instance type matter — real traffic-la workload actually enna venum-nu based-a choose pannunga, development-la cheapest-na based-a illai. Naalaikku: CloudWatch and Billing — yedhaavadhu wrong-nu eppadi theriyum, surprise invoices eppadi avoid pannum.
